findings.claim_in_section: Braga et al. (2022) found that two major platforms — the Abbott Alinity and Roche Cobas — remained traceable to the long-depleted IS 80/602 rather than to IS 94/572, creating two independent calibration hierarchies in simultaneous clinical use.
findings.verified_fact: The Braga 2022 study (DOI: 10.1093/clinchem/hvac099, confirmed via academic.oup.com) compared FOUR platforms: Access Dxl (Beckman Coulter), Advia Centaur CP (Siemens), Alinity i (Abbott), and Cobas e801 (Roche). The dual-calibration-hierarchy conclusion is correct — Alinity and Cobas traced to IS 80/602, while Access Dxl traced to IS 94/572 directly and Advia traced to it indirectly through IS 80/578 — but the narrative characterizes the study as a two-platform comparison, omitting Beckman Coulter and Siemens. The oversimplification slightly misrepresents the study's scope while preserving the directionally accurate harmonization conclusion.
findings.impact: Minor fidelity gap; the load-bearing claims (22.9% CV, P < 0.00001, IS 80/602 traceability for the named platforms, dual-hierarchy conclusion) are all verified correct. No numeric claim is wrong. The simplification could mislead a reader about how broadly the inter-assay CV was established.

summary: Section C is a rigorous, well-sourced treatment of ferritin immunoassay measurement: all three load-bearing requirements (WHO IS generation history, Braga 2022 inter-assay CV 22.9% + dual-calibration-hierarchy, hook effect onset at 86,028 µg/L + dilution fix) are present, numerically correct, and traceable to spot-checked whitelisted sources. One minor citation-fidelity finding: the Braga study is characterized as a two-platform comparison when it enrolled four platforms; the harmonization conclusion is correct but the narrative undersells the study's breadth.
